name: LinkedinAdsMCP
title: LinkedIn Ads
description: Run LinkedIn ad campaigns. Find targeting, create campaigns and image ads as drafts, pause them, read their results.
whenToUse: Pick to advertise on LinkedIn: find an ad account and the targeting to use (locations, seniorities, industries, job functions, companies), create a campaign and its image ads, pause it or lower its budget, and read spend and results per campaign. Campaigns are created as drafts and this node never switches one on, so nothing it does spends more. Attach it via a service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly to list the ad accounts.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger. When the graph runs this node it lists the ad accounts the credential can reach.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The ad accounts, or LinkedIn's reason it could not list them

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: linkedin
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. package.yaml, nodes/, credentials/ and shared/, nothing else.
#
# LinkedIn's Marketing API: ad accounts, targeting, campaigns, image ads and their results. The
# operations were chosen from IBM's LinkedIn bundle (`LinkedIn_1.0.32.ssi`) by
# docs/SSI_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md; every endpoint is from LinkedIn's own versioned docs, never the
# bundle, which calls the retired `/v2/adCampaignsV2`.
#
# LinkedIn never issues a token to an app alone. A person approves the app once and what that
# leaves behind is a refresh token, so this package is the first on `oauth2RefreshToken`.

name: linkedin
displayName: LinkedIn
description: LinkedIn ads for Unoverse
version: 1.0.0
category: communication

features:
  - Find ad accounts and targeting (locations, seniorities, industries, companies)
  - Create campaigns, created as drafts, and image ads
  - Pause a campaign or lower its budget; switching on is a separate node, for a task that asks a person first
  - Read spend and results per campaign

# The API, and the host that both mints tokens and takes uploads. `*` is for the image a caller
# hands over by url: that call carries no credential, so it has nothing to leak, and the
# executor stops matching `*` the moment one is added (as aws-s3's upload).
allowedHosts:
  - api.linkedin.com
  - www.linkedin.com
  - "*"

requires:
  credential: [oauth2RefreshToken]
  transport: [json, headers, binary]
  # An upload is processed before an ad may use it, so create_ad waits on it.
  poll: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.2.0"

credentials.linkedinOAuth.yaml:
# The SHAPE only; values live encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe.

name: linkedinOAuth
displayName: LinkedIn
description: >-
  A LinkedIn developer app and a refresh token a person made for it once. The executor trades
  the refresh token for a short-lived access token at run time and caches it, so this acts as
  that person's approval of the app, with nobody signed in.
documentationUrl: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/programmatic-refresh-tokens

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: From the app's Auth tab in the LinkedIn Developer Portal

  - name: clientSecret
    displayName: Client Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: From the app's Auth tab in the LinkedIn Developer Portal

  - name: refreshToken
    displayName: Refresh Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: >-
      Made once by a person who manages the ad account, with the scopes rw_ads and
      r_ads_reporting. It lasts a year; make a new one before it runs out.

shared.api.yaml:
# What every LinkedIn call shares: how it authenticates, and the two headers every versioned
# call needs.
#
# The refresh-token exchange. The executor mints the token, form-encodes the request, caches it
# per refresh token until it expires, and refreshes once on a 401.
credential: &credential
  scheme: oauth2RefreshToken
  tokenUrl: https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken
  clientId: "{{ credentials.linkedinOAuth.clientId }}"
  clientSecret: "{{ credentials.linkedinOAuth.clientSecret }}"
  refreshToken: "{{ credentials.linkedinOAuth.refreshToken }}"

# LinkedIn retires a version a year after it ships, and an unknown or retired one is refused,
# so this is bumped here, once, for every call.
headers: &headers
  Linkedin-Version: "202609"
  X-Restli-Protocol-Version: "2.0.0"

# A partial update is a POST that says so in a header; nothing else tells LinkedIn it is not a
# create.
patch: &patch
  Linkedin-Version: "202609"
  X-Restli-Protocol-Version: "2.0.0"
  X-RestLi-Method: PARTIAL_UPDATE
shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before it reaches LinkedIn. The wording
# IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing is a
# behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.

linkedin:
  name: LinkedIn Ads
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: >-
    Run LinkedIn ad campaigns: find ad accounts and targeting, create campaigns and image ads as
    drafts, pause them or lower their budget, and read spend and results.
  instructions: |-
    LINKEDIN ADS PROTOCOL:
    - Start with list_ad_accounts. Every other tool takes its account id, and create_campaign and create_ad take its organization and currency.
    - Targeting values are URNs. Find them with find_targeting before create_campaign; never guess one.
    - create_campaign makes a DRAFT, which spends nothing. Switching a campaign on, or raising its budget, is a person's yes and is never done here.
    - Facets combine as AND, values within a facet as OR.
    - LinkedIn tools may not be used to discriminate based on personal characteristics such as gender, age, race, or ethnicity.
    - A tool that fails carries LinkedIn's reason. Say so rather than claiming it worked.
  methods:
    list_ad_accounts:
      description: >-
        List the active ad accounts you can manage, with id, currency and the company page its
        ads are posted as.
      input:
        type: object
        properties: {}

    find_targeting:
      description: >-
        Find the targeting values for one facet, by search text or, with no text, all of them.
        Facets: locations, seniorities, industries, jobFunctions, titles, employers,
        staffCountRanges.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          facet:
            type: string
            enum: [locations, seniorities, industries, jobFunctions, titles, employers, staffCountRanges]
            description: The kind of targeting.
          query:
            type: string
            description: >-
              Search text, e.g. "United Arab Emirates", "retail", "Emirates NBD". Needed for
              locations, titles and employers; leave out to list every seniority, job function
              or company size.
        required: [facet]

    list_campaigns:
      description: >-
        List an ad account's campaigns that are on, paused or drafts, with status, daily budget
        and objective.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id, from list_ad_accounts.
        required: [account_id]

    create_campaign:
      description: >-
        Create a campaign, as a DRAFT that spends nothing until a person switches it on.
        Give it a name, a daily budget in the account's currency, an objective and its
        targeting.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          organization:
            type: string
            description: The account's organization, from list_ad_accounts.
          name:
            type: string
            description: What the campaign is for, e.g. "Gulf retail VPs, October".
          currency:
            type: string
            description: The account's currency, from list_ad_accounts.
          daily_budget:
            type: number
            description: Most to spend per day, in the account's currency.
          objective:
            type: string
            enum: [WEBSITE_VISIT, BRAND_AWARENESS]
            description: WEBSITE_VISIT (clicks to a page, the default) or BRAND_AWARENESS (to be seen).
          targeting:
            type: object
            description: >-
              Facet name to a list of URNs from find_targeting, e.g. { "locations":
              ["urn:li:geo:104305776"], "seniorities": ["urn:li:seniority:7"] }.
            properties:
              locations: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              seniorities: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              industries: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              jobFunctions: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              titles: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              employers: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
              staffCountRanges: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
        required: [account_id, organization, name, currency, daily_budget, targeting]

    create_ad:
      description: >-
        Create an image ad in a campaign, posted as the account's company page: the words, an
        image by its https url, a headline, and the page it links to.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          campaign_id:
            type: string
            description: The campaign's id, from create_campaign or list_campaigns.
          organization:
            type: string
            description: The account's organization, from list_ad_accounts.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The words above the image. Keep it under 150 characters for the feed.
          image_url:
            type: string
            description: An https url of a JPG, PNG or GIF.
          headline:
            type: string
            description: The headline under the image, up to 70 characters.
          landing_page:
            type: string
            description: The https page the ad links to.
          call_to_action:
            type: string
            enum: [LEARN_MORE, SIGN_UP, REGISTER, DOWNLOAD, REQUEST_DEMO, SUBSCRIBE, APPLY, JOIN, ATTEND]
            description: The button's label (optional).
        required: [account_id, campaign_id, organization, text, image_url, headline, landing_page]

    change_campaign:
      description: >-
        Pause or archive a campaign, or lower its daily budget. It never switches a campaign on
        or raises a budget: those spend more, and are a person's yes.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          campaign_id:
            type: string
            description: The campaign's id.
          status:
            type: string
            enum: [PAUSED, ARCHIVED]
            description: Pause it, or archive it (optional).
          daily_budget:
            type: number
            description: A lower daily budget (optional), in the account's currency.
        required: [account_id, campaign_id]

    report:
      description: >-
        Spend and results per campaign in an ad account, from a start date (YYYY-MM-DD, default
        30 days ago) to today or an end date. Optionally only some campaigns.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          account_id:
            type: string
            description: The ad account's id.
          since:
            type: string
            description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD (optional, default 30 days ago).
          until:
            type: string
            description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (optional, default today).
          campaign_ids:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            description: Only these campaigns (optional).
        required: [account_id]
shared.shape.yaml:
# The ad accounts, bounded to what a caller decides with: its id for every other tool, its
# currency for a budget, and `organization`, the company page its ads are posted as.
#
# Here once, because the graph run (events.yaml) and the list_ad_accounts tool answer with the
# same shape.
accounts: &accounts >-
  return {
    ok: true,
    accounts: (response.elements || []).map(a => ({
      id: String(a.id),
      name: a.name,
      currency: a.currency,
      organization: a.reference || null,
      status: a.status,
      serving: a.servingStatuses || [],
      test: !!a.test
    }))
  }

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row, one connector: the accounts, in the same shape list_ad_accounts answers with.

- emit: output
  from: response
  value: { $ref: shape#accounts }
files.api/run.yaml:
# Triggered by the graph, this node lists the ad accounts the credential can reach: the read
# that proves the refresh-token exchange works, and the ids every tool needs.

- name: accounts
  method: GET
  url: "https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts?q=search&search=(status:(values:List(ACTIVE)))"
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  headers: { $ref: api#headers }
  transport: json
files.api/service.yaml:
# The MCP methods an agent can call, over LinkedIn's versioned Marketing API (shared/api.yaml
# holds the version). Seven, from the bundle's 42 operations: what an agent running ads does,
# and nothing that creates accounts, manages their users or deletes.
#
# REST.LI QUERIES are built in the url, never in `query:`. Their parentheses, colons and commas
# are syntax and must reach LinkedIn as written, while a URN inside them is a value and is
# encoded. A query map would encode both.
#
# IDS COME BACK IN A HEADER. A create answers 201 with an empty body and the new id in
# `x-restli-id`, so every create is read with `transport: headers`.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for LinkedIn Ads
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#linkedin }

list_ad_accounts:
  description: >-
    List the active ad accounts you can manage, with id, currency and the company page its ads
    are posted as.
  calls:
    - name: accounts
      method: GET
      url: "https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts?q=search&search=(status:(values:List(ACTIVE)))"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
  returns: { $ref: shape#accounts }

find_targeting:
  description: >-
    Find the targeting values for one facet, by search text or, with no text, all of them.
    Facets: locations, seniorities, industries, jobFunctions, titles, employers,
    staffCountRanges.
  calls:
    - name: search
      when: "return !!params.query"
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adTargetingEntities?q=typeahead&queryVersion=QUERY_USES_URNS'
          + '&facet=' + encodeURIComponent('urn:li:adTargetingFacet:' + params.facet)
          + '&query=' + encodeURIComponent(params.query)
          + '&locale=(language:en,country:US)'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
    - name: all
      when: "return !params.query"
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adTargetingEntities?q=adTargetingFacet&queryVersion=QUERY_USES_URNS'
          + '&facet=' + encodeURIComponent('urn:li:adTargetingFacet:' + params.facet)
          + '&locale=(language:en,country:US)'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      facet: params.facet,
      values: ((calls.search || calls.all || {}).elements || []).slice(0, 50).map(e => ({ urn: e.urn, name: e.name })),
      has_more: ((calls.search || calls.all || {}).elements || []).length > 50
    }

list_campaigns:
  description: >-
    List an ad account's campaigns that are on, paused or drafts, with status, daily budget and
    objective.
  calls:
    - name: campaigns
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id)
          + '/adCampaigns?q=search&search=(status:(values:List(ACTIVE,PAUSED,DRAFT)))&sortOrder=DESCENDING'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      campaigns: (response.elements || []).map(c => ({
        id: String(c.id),
        name: c.name,
        status: c.status,
        objective: c.objectiveType || null,
        daily_budget: c.dailyBudget || null,
        campaign_group: c.campaignGroup,
        serving: c.servingStatuses || []
      })),
      has_more: !!((response.metadata || {}).nextPageToken)
    }

create_campaign:
  description: >-
    Create a campaign, as a DRAFT that spends nothing until a person switches it on. Give
    it a name, a daily budget in the account's currency, an objective and its targeting.
  calls:
    # Its own campaign group, so a campaign's budget and status are never shared with another's
    # by accident. The group is on; the campaign inside it is a draft, and a draft never serves.
    - name: group
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/adCampaignGroups'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      body: >-
        return {
          account: 'urn:li:sponsoredAccount:' + params.account_id,
          name: String(params.name),
          runSchedule: { start: Date.now() },
          status: 'ACTIVE'
        }
      transport: headers
    - name: campaign
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/adCampaigns'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      # Targeting is AND across facets and OR within one, which is LinkedIn's own reading of
      # targetingCriteria. The interface locale is required on every campaign's targeting.
      body: >-
        return {
          account: 'urn:li:sponsoredAccount:' + params.account_id,
          campaignGroup: 'urn:li:sponsoredCampaignGroup:' + String(calls.group['x-restli-id']).split(':').at(-1),
          associatedEntity: String(params.organization).startsWith('urn:') ? params.organization : 'urn:li:organization:' + params.organization,
          name: String(params.name),
          type: 'SPONSORED_UPDATES',
          format: 'STANDARD_UPDATE',
          objectiveType: params.objective || 'WEBSITE_VISIT',
          costType: params.objective === 'BRAND_AWARENESS' ? 'CPM' : 'CPC',
          optimizationTargetType: params.objective === 'BRAND_AWARENESS' ? 'MAX_IMPRESSION' : 'MAX_CLICK',
          creativeSelection: 'OPTIMIZED',
          dailyBudget: { amount: String(params.daily_budget), currencyCode: params.currency },
          locale: { country: 'US', language: 'en' },
          audienceExpansionEnabled: false,
          offsiteDeliveryEnabled: false,
          politicalIntent: 'NOT_POLITICAL',
          runSchedule: { start: Date.now() },
          targetingCriteria: {
            include: {
              and: Object.entries(params.targeting || {})
                .filter(e => Array.isArray(e[1]) && e[1].length > 0)
                .map(e => ({ or: Object.fromEntries([['urn:li:adTargetingFacet:' + e[0], e[1]]]) }))
                .concat([{ or: { 'urn:li:adTargetingFacet:interfaceLocales': ['urn:li:locale:en_US'] } }])
            }
          },
          status: 'DRAFT'
        }
      transport: headers
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      campaign_id: String(calls.campaign['x-restli-id']).split(':').at(-1),
      campaign_group_id: String(calls.group['x-restli-id']).split(':').at(-1),
      status: 'DRAFT'
    }

create_ad:
  description: >-
    Create an image ad in a campaign, posted as the account's company page: the words, an image
    by its https url, a headline, and the page it links to.
  calls:
    # The image, fetched with no credential (allowedHosts `*`), handed on as bytes.
    - name: source
      method: GET
      url: "{{ params.image_url }}"
      transport: binary
      timeoutMs: 60000
    - name: init
      method: POST
      url: "https://api.linkedin.com/rest/images?action=initializeUpload"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      body: >-
        return {
          initializeUploadRequest: {
            owner: String(params.organization).startsWith('urn:') ? params.organization : 'urn:li:organization:' + params.organization
          }
        }
      transport: json
    - name: put
      method: PUT
      url: "return calls.init.value.uploadUrl"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers:
        Content-Type: "return (calls.source || {}).contentType || 'image/png'"
      encoding: binary
      body: "return calls.source"
      transport: headers
    # LinkedIn processes an upload before an ad may use it.
    - name: ready
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/images/' + encodeURIComponent(calls.init.value.image)"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
      poll:
        url: "return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/images/' + encodeURIComponent(calls.init.value.image)"
        until: "return response.status === 'AVAILABLE'"
        failed: "return response.status === 'PROCESSING_FAILED'"
        message: "return 'LinkedIn could not process the image: ' + response.status"
        intervalMs: 2000
        maxAttempts: 15
    # The post and the ad in one call. `intendedStatus: ACTIVE` sends it for review; it serves
    # only once its campaign is on.
    - name: creative
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id) + '/creatives?action=createInline'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      body: >-
        return {
          creative: {
            campaign: 'urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:' + params.campaign_id,
            intendedStatus: 'ACTIVE',
            inlineContent: {
              post: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
                adContext: { dscAdAccount: 'urn:li:sponsoredAccount:' + params.account_id, dscStatus: 'ACTIVE' },
                author: String(params.organization).startsWith('urn:') ? params.organization : 'urn:li:organization:' + params.organization,
                commentary: String(params.text),
                visibility: 'PUBLIC',
                lifecycleState: 'PUBLISHED',
                isReshareDisabledByAuthor: false,
                contentLandingPage: params.landing_page,
                contentCallToActionLabel: params.call_to_action,
                content: { media: { title: params.headline, id: calls.init.value.image } }
              }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
            }
          }
        }
      transport: headers
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      creative_id: String(calls.creative['x-restli-id'] || ''),
      image: calls.init.value.image
    }

change_campaign:
  description: >-
    Pause or archive a campaign, or lower its daily budget. It never switches a campaign on or
    raises a budget: those spend more, and are a person's yes.
  calls:
    # What it is now, so a budget can be checked as lower and its currency kept.
    - name: current
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id)
          + '/adCampaigns/' + encodeURIComponent(params.campaign_id)
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
    - name: patch
      when: >-
        return (!params.status || ['PAUSED', 'ARCHIVED'].indexOf(params.status) !== -1)
          && (!params.daily_budget || Number(params.daily_budget) <= Number(((calls.current || {}).dailyBudget || {}).amount || 0))
          && !!(params.status || params.daily_budget)
      method: POST
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAccounts/' + encodeURIComponent(params.account_id)
          + '/adCampaigns/' + encodeURIComponent(params.campaign_id)
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#patch }
      body: >-
        return {
          patch: {
            $set: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
              status: params.status,
              dailyBudget: params.daily_budget
                ? { amount: String(params.daily_budget), currencyCode: ((calls.current || {}).dailyBudget || {}).currencyCode }
                : undefined
            }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
          }
        }
      transport: headers
  # Refused rather than thrown, so an agent reads why and does not retry the same thing.
  returns: >-
    return calls.patch
      ? { ok: true, campaign_id: String(params.campaign_id), status: params.status || (calls.current || {}).status, daily_budget: params.daily_budget || ((calls.current || {}).dailyBudget || {}).amount }
      : { ok: false, error: 'change_campaign only pauses, archives or lowers a budget; switching on or raising a budget needs a person\'s yes' }

report:
  description: >-
    Spend and results per campaign in an ad account, from a start date (YYYY-MM-DD, default 30
    days ago) to today or an end date. Optionally only some campaigns.
  calls:
    - name: analytics
      method: GET
      url: >-
        return 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adAnalytics?q=analytics&pivot=CAMPAIGN&timeGranularity=ALL'
          + '&dateRange=(start:(year:' + Number(String(params.since || Date.iso(Date.now() - 30 * 86400000).split('T')[0]).split('-')[0])
          + ',month:' + Number(String(params.since || Date.iso(Date.now() - 30 * 86400000).split('T')[0]).split('-')[1])
          + ',day:' + Number(String(params.since || Date.iso(Date.now() - 30 * 86400000).split('T')[0]).split('-')[2]) + ')'
          + (params.until
              ? ',end:(year:' + Number(String(params.until).split('-')[0]) + ',month:' + Number(String(params.until).split('-')[1]) + ',day:' + Number(String(params.until).split('-')[2]) + ')'
              : '')
          + ')'
          + '&accounts=List(' + encodeURIComponent('urn:li:sponsoredAccount:' + params.account_id) + ')'
          + ((params.campaign_ids || []).length
              ? '&campaigns=List(' + params.campaign_ids.map(id => encodeURIComponent('urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:' + id)).join(',') + ')'
              : '')
          + '&fields=impressions,clicks,landingPageClicks,costInLocalCurrency,externalWebsiteConversions,oneClickLeads,approximateMemberReach,pivotValues,dateRange'
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      headers: { $ref: api#headers }
      transport: json
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      campaigns: (response.elements || []).map(r => ({
        campaign_id: String((r.pivotValues || [''])[0]).split(':').at(-1),
        spend: Number(r.costInLocalCurrency || 0),
        impressions: r.impressions || 0,
        reach: r.approximateMemberReach || 0,
        clicks: r.clicks || 0,
        landing_page_clicks: r.landingPageClicks || 0,
        conversions: r.externalWebsiteConversions || 0,
        leads: r.oneClickLeads || 0
      }))
    }

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. When the graph runs this node it lists the ad accounts the credential can reach.

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: The ad accounts, or LinkedIn's reason it could not list them

credentials:
  - name: linkedinOAuth
    required: true
    displayName: LinkedIn

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [list_ad_accounts, find_targeting, list_campaigns, create_campaign, create_ad, change_campaign, report]
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: find ad accounts and targeting, create campaigns and image ads,
      pause them or lower their budget, read their results.
files.node.yaml:
type: LinkedinAdsMCP
kind: PromiseNode
name: LinkedIn Ads
category: Go To Market
color: "#0A66C2"
# Attached to an agent over a service edge rather than wired in sequence.
template: service
description: Run LinkedIn ad campaigns. Find targeting, create campaigns and image ads as drafts, pause them, read their results.
whenToUse: >
  Pick to advertise on LinkedIn: find an ad account and the targeting to use (locations,
  seniorities, industries, job functions, companies), create a campaign and its image ads,
  pause it or lower its budget, and read spend and results per campaign. Campaigns are created
  as drafts and this node never switches one on, so nothing it does spends more. Attach it via a
  service edge to an agent, or trigger it directly to list the ad accounts.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Not cacheable: campaigns and their results change underneath us, and the write methods
  # spend money when a campaign is on, which reuse would silently skip.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# The READ path, because it is the one that proves the refresh-token exchange and the version
# header work. The write methods are deliberately not the fixture: they would leave real
# campaigns behind. Try them on a test ad account, which never serves and never bills.
testData:
  config: {}

  inputs:
    input: {}

  expect:
    # Any account answers this. Asserting a count would tie the fixture to one company's ads.
    output: >-
      return output.output.ok === true && Array.isArray(output.output.accounts)
